_comment: Derived from what Antigravity reported about itself, then corrected against the real files on disk. Three things it proposed did not survive: `action.where` tested the ARRAY ENTRIES of tool_calls, which carry only {name,args} and no type; `title` mapped to USER_INPUT content, but the walk runs backwards so that yields the LAST message, not a name; and `content` is wrapped in <USER_REQUEST> with metadata appended.
_mark: TRACED from the real asset, never drawn: icon.png inside Antigravity's own app.asar (Programs/Antigravity/resources), vectorised by following the contour of its alpha channel, simplified to 27 points and inset to 92% so the badge breathes like the others. Compared side by side with the source PNG at 24px and 80px before shipping; a hand-drawn arch was tried first, was visibly fatter with stubby legs, and was discarded.
_tree: Transcripts are buried three levels down: <root>/<sessionId>/.system_generated/logs/. One listing per session directory rather than a crawl. `idFrom: dir` because no line carries a session id — the directory name IS the id.
_filePattern: transcript.jsonl, not .jsonl: transcript_full.jsonl sits beside it with untruncated tool output. Only tool NAMES and human turns are read here, so the truncated file carries everything needed at half the bytes.
_fields: Measured on a real transcript: every line carries step_index, source, type, status, created_at. There is no model, no cwd and no branch at line level — a working directory shows up only inside some tool arguments, which is not the session's project. Absent stays absent rather than being guessed from an argument.
_shellWrite: run_command is 3300 of the tool calls in the real transcripts on this machine, against 1366 write_to_file. The command string sits in args.CommandLine, stored wrapped in its own quote pair. The PATTERNS live in the app (lib/shellWrites), never here: a connector is data and may not carry a regex.
_humanTurn: USER_INPUT lines are the person. Tool results are their own line types (LIST_DIRECTORY, VIEW_FILE, RUN_COMMAND), so no notWhen clause is needed. The text is clipped to what sits inside <USER_REQUEST>, which drops the appended local-time and settings-change metadata.
